title: Unsafe Bypassing of Compiler Borrow Verification (Ad-Hoc Pointers)
pattern: Casting read-only references to raw mutable pointers inside `unsafe` blocks to bypass the borrow checker's aliasing rules.
why_bad: It actively violates Rust's core memory safety guarantees. Mutating data through a shared reference (`&T`) is undefined behavior, as the compiler assumes the underlying memory is immutable, leading to memory corruption.
detection: An `unsafe` block containing reference-to-raw-pointer casts (`as *const T as *mut T`) that mutate fields.
counterexample: Low-level synchronization primitives implementing standard interior mutability (such as `UnsafeCell`) that are thoroughly audited. `Context-dependent`.
source: *Rust for Rustaceans*, Chapter 9 (Unsafe) / *Building Secure and Reliable Systems*, Chapter 12.
